messages:
maria: Ran an Nsight timeline capture on the 8xA100 testbed this morning, focusing on tfwd path + kv-cache prefetch. link: https://internal.nvidia/captures/1870012345 :eyes:

sam: Nice — did you capture with per-stream memcpy tracing? those H2D spikes can hide behind other kernels if streams overlap.

maria: yeah captured per-stream. main symptom: repeated GPU idle gaps ~200-600us between micro-batches. Nsight shows a recurring H2D memcpy on stream 2 right before the model forward, then an NCCL all-reduce bar that waits for buffers. timeline snapshot: ``[memcpy H2D] -> [compute chunk] -> [nccl allreduce wait] -> idle``

jordana: can you paste the minimal log snippet from the custom timers? e.g., kv_prefetch, forward_start, allreduce_start, allreduce_end, forward_end.

maria: paste below (trimmed):
```
KV_PREFETCH_START 0.000123
KV_PREFETCH_END   0.000255
FORWARD_START     0.000260
ALLREDUCE_START   0.000950
ALLREDUCE_END     0.001200
FORWARD_END       0.001210
```
This repeats per micro-batch, roughly 900us compute window but allreduce aligns late because prefetch memcpy pushes data onto stream that blocks NCCL progress on the default stream.

ryan: That ordering smells like prefetch using blocking cudaMemcpyAsync or pinned memory fallback. Are we still falling back to host staging for some kv pages?

maria: Confirmed — small fraction of pages hit the staging path due to mis-sized prefetch chunks. Kernel selector picked the 32KB memcpy kernel which ends up serialized. Also we were launching prefetch on stream 2 while nccl on stream 0 expects data on different stream and waits for event.

sam: Two quick experiments to try: 1) move KV prefetch to the same non-blocking stream as compute and use cudaEvent to signal nccl start, 2) force NCCL async progress (NCCL_ASYNC=1) and see overlap change.

jordana: Another angle: change batching heuristic to avoid issuing prefetch for the last token chunk when sequence length < threshold (no benefit vs added overhead). Add a guard: ``if (seq_rem < PREFETCH_MIN) skip_prefetch()``

maria: I tried 1) and 2) on a copy of the run. Results: overlap improved but still ~120us tail waits. Timeline shows periodic small H2D memcpy on stream 0 that looks like metadata copies (not the big kv pages).

ryan: Could be kernel selection for small memcpy falling back to single-thread path. We have a fast-path for >64KB, medium for 4-64KB, slow for <4KB. Those metadata copies might be <4KB and expensive. We can aggregate them into one batched memcpy in prefetch code.

maria: Agreed. Quick patch: batch metadata into a single 128B -> 8KB chunk per shard. After patch, Nsight shows those micro-copies vanish, tail wait reduced to ~30-40us on avg.

sam: Nice! Any regressions in latency p99?

maria: p50 unchanged, p95 down 15%, p99 down ~8%. Throughput unaffected. Attach perf diff: `perf/1870012345/summary.txt` (private link).

jordana: We should also add a timer around kernel_selector->pick for small memcpy cases so we can alert if selection falls back to slow path at scale. Add metric `memcpy_slow_path_count` and surface in console.

maria: On it. Also adding a guard in batching heuristic to avoid prefetch on tail micro-batches reduced number of nccl fragments by ~1.2x.

ci-bot: Deploy triggered: deploy/eng-runtime/kv-prefetch-agg/1870012400 started by maria.

ryan: Quick note — when enabling NCCL_ASYNC we saw less overlap for some configs due to driver behavior on older Tesla images. Keep fallback to sync if hw/drivers mismatch. Add runtime toggle.

maria: Plan: land metadata aggregation + batching guard + small probe metric. Run full 8x and 4x baseline sweep tomorrow with Nsight capture and nvprof sampling for kernel selection counts. Follow-ups: adjust kernel thresholds if slow_path_count exceeds threshold.

sam: Great. If you want I can take the nvprof collection and generate a small script to parse memcpy kernel names across runs.

maria: Yes please, assign to you. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
